icons.name: Staphylococcus
icons.description: Gram-positive cocci in grape-like clusters. Coloured violet, after the Gram stain.

icons.name: Escherichia coli
icons.description: Gram-negative bacillus with a double envelope, peritrichous flagella and pili. Coloured pink, after the Gram stain.

icons.name: Streptococcus
icons.description: Gram-positive cocci in chains (e.g. group A and group B streptococci). Coloured violet, after the Gram stain.

icons.name: Pneumococcus
icons.description: Lancet-shaped Gram-positive diplococci surrounded by a polysaccharide capsule.

icons.name: Meningococcus
icons.description: Kidney-shaped Gram-negative diplococci. Coloured pink, after the Gram stain.

icons.name: Mycobacterium tuberculosis
icons.description: Slender, beaded acid-fast bacilli in a cord. Coloured red, after the Ziehl–Neelsen stain.

icons.name: Biofilm
icons.description: Bacteria embedded in an extracellular matrix on a surface, with free-swimming planktonic cells above.

icons.name: Kingella kingae
icons.description: Plump Gram-negative coccobacilli in pairs and short chains. Coloured pink, after the Gram stain.

icons.name: Bordetella pertussis
icons.description: Small Gram-negative coccobacilli with fimbriae, and pertussis toxin molecules (orange, A subunit on a ring of five B subunits).

icons.name: Listeria monocytogenes
icons.description: Gram-positive rods inside a host cell, propelled by actin comet tails, one pushing out in a membrane protrusion.

icons.name: Treponema pallidum
icons.description: Tightly coiled spirochaetes.

icons.name: Pseudomonas aeruginosa
icons.description: Slender Gram-negative bacilli, each with a single polar flagellum. Coloured pink, after the Gram stain.

icons.name: Klebsiella
icons.description: A pair of plump, non-motile Gram-negative bacilli inside a thick polysaccharide capsule.

icons.name: Salmonella
icons.description: Gram-negative bacilli invading the gut epithelium: one swimming with peritrichous flagella, one triggering membrane ruffles on an enterocyte, and one inside a Salmonella-containing vacuole.

icons.name: Clostridioides difficile
icons.description: Large Gram-positive bacilli: a vegetative cell with peritrichous flagella, a cell with a subterminal spore, and free spores (coloured green, after the spore stain).

icons.name: Haemophilus influenzae
icons.description: Small, pleomorphic Gram-negative coccobacilli, each in a polysaccharide capsule (as in type b, Hib).

icons.name: Mycoplasma pneumoniae
icons.description: Flask-shaped bacteria with no cell wall, attaching by their tip organelles among the cilia of the respiratory epithelium.

icons.name: Campylobacter
icons.description: Curved, S-shaped Gram-negative rods with a single flagellum at each pole.

icons.name: Clostridium tetani
icons.description: Slender Gram-positive rods with round terminal spores, the "drumstick" shape, beside a vegetative rod with peritrichous flagella.

icons.name: Corynebacterium diphtheriae
icons.description: Club-shaped Gram-positive rods in V and L shapes ("Chinese letters") after snapping division, with metachromatic granules at their poles.

icons.name: Chlamydia
icons.description: An epithelial cell holding a Chlamydia inclusion packed with reticulate bodies (larger, dividing) and elementary bodies (small, infectious), its nucleus pushed aside; elementary bodies are released.

icons.name: Borrelia
icons.description: Long, loosely and irregularly coiled spirochaetes, as in Lyme disease.

icons.name: Enterococcus
icons.description: Oval Gram-positive cocci in pairs and short chains.

icons.name: SARS-CoV-2
icons.description: Enveloped coronavirus with spike (S) glycoproteins and membrane (M) proteins.

icons.name: Adenovirus
icons.description: Non-enveloped icosahedral capsid with hexon capsomeres, penton bases and protruding fibres.

icons.name: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)
icons.description: Enveloped pneumovirus with fusion (F, orange) and attachment (G, blue) glycoproteins and a helical nucleocapsid.

icons.name: Influenza virus
icons.description: Enveloped orthomyxovirus with haemagglutinin (HA, blue) and neuraminidase (NA, red) spikes and eight RNA segments.

icons.name: Herpesvirus (e.g. CMV)
icons.description: Enveloped virus with glycoprotein spikes, a tegument layer and an icosahedral capsid.

icons.name: Bacteriophage
icons.description: Tailed phage with an icosahedral head, contractile tail sheath, baseplate and tail fibres.

icons.name: Rotavirus
icons.description: Non-enveloped, triple-layered wheel-like capsid with VP4 spikes.

icons.name: Enterovirus
icons.description: Small non-enveloped icosahedral capsid (picornavirus), also suitable for parechovirus, poliovirus and rhinovirus.

icons.name: Measles virus
icons.description: Pleomorphic enveloped paramyxovirus with haemagglutinin (H, blue) and fusion (F, orange) glycoproteins and a helical nucleocapsid.

icons.name: HIV
icons.description: Enveloped retrovirus with sparse Env (gp120/gp41) spike trimers, a matrix layer and a cone-shaped capsid holding two RNA genomes and reverse transcriptase.

icons.name: Norovirus
icons.description: Non-enveloped calicivirus: an icosahedral capsid whose arch-like protruding dimers ring 32 cup-shaped depressions.

icons.name: Hepatitis B virus
icons.description: Dane particle: an envelope studded with surface antigen (HBsAg) around an icosahedral core (HBcAg) holding partly double-stranded circular DNA and its polymerase.

icons.name: Mpox virus
icons.description: Brick-shaped orthopoxvirus in section: surface tubules round the membrane, a dumbbell-shaped core holding the DNA, and two lateral bodies.

icons.name: Dengue virus
icons.description: Mature flavivirus with its smooth surface of E-protein dimers lying flat in a herringbone of rafts, coloured by domain (I red, II yellow, III blue); also stands for Zika, yellow fever and other flaviviruses.

icons.name: Parvovirus B19
icons.description: Small non-enveloped icosahedral capsid with spikes at the 3-fold axes and pores ringed by canyons at the 5-fold axes.

icons.name: Rabies virus
icons.description: Bullet-shaped lyssavirus: glycoprotein spikes over its envelope, except at the flat base, around the coiled helical nucleocapsid.

icons.name: Hepatitis C virus
icons.description: Enveloped hepacivirus with E1/E2 glycoprotein heterodimers, round a core holding its single-stranded RNA genome.

icons.name: CMV-infected cell
icons.description: An enlarged cell infected with cytomegalovirus: a large intranuclear inclusion ringed by a clear halo ("owl's eye") and small cytoplasmic inclusions, beside two normal cells.

icons.name: Candida (budding yeast)
icons.description: Yeast cell with a daughter bud, thick cell wall, vacuole, nucleus and bud scar.

icons.name: Aspergillus
icons.description: Mould with septate branching hyphae and a conidiophore bearing chains of conidia.

icons.name: Cryptococcus
icons.description: Round yeast cells with a thick polysaccharide capsule, one with a narrow-necked bud, as seen on India ink staining.

icons.name: Pneumocystis jirovecii
icons.description: Pneumocystis cysts (asci) holding eight intracystic bodies, one collapsed into a cup shape, among small trophic forms.

icons.name: Rhizopus (mucormycosis)
icons.description: Broad, ribbon-like hyphae with few septa, rooted by rhizoids, with sporangiophores bearing a sporangium full of spores, a burst one showing its columella, and a young one.

icons.name: Malaria (Plasmodium)
icons.description: Red blood cells infected with Plasmodium: ring forms with chromatin dots, and a banana-shaped gametocyte.

icons.name: Toxoplasma gondii
icons.description: Crescent-shaped tachyzoite with apical conoid, rhoptries (orange), micronemes (yellow) and nucleus.

icons.name: Giardia
icons.description: Giardia trophozoite from the ventral side: pear-shaped, with two nuclei, a ventral adhesive disc, median bodies and four pairs of flagella.

icons.name: Mosquito
icons.description: Anopheles mosquito at rest, with the body and proboscis held in a line at an angle to the surface, long palps and spotted wings.

icons.name: Threadworm
icons.description: Enterobius vermicularis: a female worm with a long pointed tail, a smaller male with a curled tail, and eggs flattened on one side, each holding a larva.

icons.name: Scabies mite
icons.description: Sarcoptes scabiei from above: a rounded body with transverse ridges and spines, short legs ending in stalked suckers at the front and long bristles at the back.

icons.name: Head louse
icons.description: Pediculus humanus capitis from above, with clawed legs for gripping hair, beside a hair carrying a nit (egg).

icons.name: Tick
icons.description: Hard (ixodid) tick from above: mouthparts at the front, a dark dorsal shield, and four pairs of legs.

icons.name: Schistosoma
icons.description: Adult schistosomes in copula: the female lying in the male's gynaecophoric canal, her ends protruding, beside an egg with a lateral spine (S. mansoni) holding a miracidium.

icons.name: Trypanosoma
icons.description: Trypomastigote among red cells: a slender body with a central nucleus and a posterior kinetoplast, its flagellum running along an undulating membrane and free beyond the anterior tip.

icons.name: Leishmania
icons.description: Leishmania amastigotes, each with a nucleus and rod-shaped kinetoplast, inside a macrophage, beside the sandfly that transmits them.

icons.name: Neutrophil
icons.description: Polymorphonuclear neutrophil with a multilobed nucleus and cytoplasmic granules.

icons.name: Macrophage
icons.description: Macrophage with pseudopodia, lysosomes and phagosomes containing engulfed bacteria.

icons.name: T cell
icons.description: Lymphocyte with a large nucleus and surface αβ T-cell receptors.

icons.name: B cell
icons.description: Lymphocyte with a large nucleus and surface B-cell receptors (membrane-bound antibody).

icons.name: Plasma cell
icons.description: Antibody-secreting cell with an eccentric clock-face nucleus, perinuclear Golgi and abundant rough endoplasmic reticulum.

icons.name: Dendritic cell
icons.description: Antigen-presenting cell with long dendritic processes.

icons.name: Natural killer cell
icons.description: Large granular lymphocyte with cytotoxic granules polarised to one side.

icons.name: Red blood cells
icons.description: Biconcave erythrocytes.

icons.name: Monocyte
icons.description: Large mononuclear cell with a horseshoe-shaped nucleus and vacuolated cytoplasm.

icons.name: Eosinophil
icons.description: Granulocyte with a bilobed nucleus and orange-red eosinophilic granules.

icons.name: Platelets
icons.description: Resting discoid platelets with granules, and an activated platelet with pseudopods.

icons.name: CD8 T cell killing an infected cell
icons.description: Cytotoxic T cell releasing granules across the immune synapse into a virus-infected target cell, which is blebbing as it dies.

icons.name: Mast cell
icons.description: Mast cell packed with granules, releasing them on one side, with IgE bound to its surface.

icons.name: Neutrophil extracellular traps
icons.description: Neutrophil releasing a web of DNA (NETs) that traps bacteria.

icons.name: Regulatory T cell
icons.description: CD4+ regulatory T cell carrying T-cell receptors and the IL-2 receptor α chain (CD25), releasing suppressive cytokines such as IL-10 and TGF-β.

icons.name: Basophil
icons.description: Granulocyte with a lobed nucleus largely hidden by large, dark basophilic granules.

icons.name: Immune synapse
icons.description: A T cell meeting an antigen-presenting cell: T-cell receptors bind peptide–MHC complexes across the narrow gap between the two cells.

icons.name: Neutrophil extravasation
icons.description: Neutrophils leaving a blood vessel: one rolling along the endothelium on selectins, one squeezing through a junction between endothelial cells (diapedesis), and one crawling through the tissue towards bacteria.

icons.name: Germinal centre
icons.description: Lymphoid follicle with a mantle of naive B cells round a germinal centre: the dark zone of dividing centroblasts and the light zone of centrocytes among follicular dendritic cells and Tfh cells.

icons.name: T helper cell subsets
icons.description: A naive CD4 T cell differentiating into four helper subsets (Th1, Th2, Th17, Tfh), each releasing its own cytokines, shown with a different shape for each subset.

icons.name: IgG antibody
icons.description: Immunoglobulin G showing heavy chains (dark blue), light chains (light blue), hinge disulphide bonds and the Fc glycan.

icons.name: IgM pentamer
icons.description: Pentameric immunoglobulin M with five antibody units joined by the J chain (orange).

icons.name: MHC class II with peptide
icons.description: MHC class II molecule (α chain lilac, β chain teal) presenting a peptide (orange) at the cell membrane.

icons.name: Cytokine and receptor
icons.description: Cytokine bound to a dimeric receptor in the cell membrane, with associated JAK kinases inside the cell and free cytokines above.

icons.name: Complement membrane attack complex
icons.description: Complement membrane attack complex: a C9 pore (pink) assembled on C5b–8 (purple), spanning a lipid bilayer.

icons.name: MHC class I
icons.description: MHC class I molecule in the cell membrane: a heavy chain (α1, α2 and α3 domains) with β2-microglobulin, presenting a short peptide in a groove closed at both ends.

icons.name: Secretory IgA
icons.description: Dimeric IgA: two antibody units joined tail to tail by the J chain and wrapped by the secretory component, as found on mucosal surfaces and in breast milk.

icons.name: Toll-like receptor
icons.description: Toll-like receptor dimer: two horseshoe-shaped leucine-rich-repeat ectodomains binding a microbial ligand (here lipopolysaccharide), each crossing the membrane to a TIR signalling domain.

icons.name: C3b opsonisation
icons.description: A bacterium coated in C3b, held by complement receptors on a phagocyte whose arms are closing around it.

icons.name: IgE on a mast cell
icons.description: IgE held by its Fc receptor (FcεRI) on a mast cell; an allergen cross-links two IgE molecules and a granule releases histamine.

icons.name: Antibody binding an epitope
icons.description: An IgG antibody binding two epitopes on the surface of an antigen with the tips of its Fab arms.

icons.name: Inflammasome
icons.description: NLRP3 inflammasome seen from above: a wheel of NLRP3 subunits (NACHT domains inside, LRR domains outside) from which an ASC filament recruits caspase-1, releasing IL-1β.

icons.name: Interferon signalling
icons.description: Type I interferon binding its receptor (IFNAR1 and IFNAR2); the receptor-bound kinases (JAK1, TYK2) phosphorylate STAT1 and STAT2, which with IRF9 (ISGF3) move into the nucleus and bind DNA.

icons.name: Complement pathways
icons.description: Complement activation on a bacterial surface by the classical (C1q on antibody), lectin (mannose-binding lectin on mannose) and alternative (C3bBb) pathways, all leading to C3 being split into C3b and C3a.

icons.name: Fc receptor binding
icons.description: A phagocyte engulfing a bacterium coated with IgG: Fcγ receptors on the phagocyte bind the antibodies' Fc regions.

icons.name: Lungs
icons.description: Lungs with trachea, bronchi and lobar fissures.

icons.name: Brain
icons.description: Brain in side view: cerebrum with sulci, cerebellum and brainstem.

icons.name: Heart
icons.description: Heart with aorta and arch vessels (red), superior vena cava and pulmonary trunk (blue), and coronary arteries.

icons.name: Kidneys and urinary tract
icons.description: Kidneys with renal pelvis, ureters, bladder and urethra.

icons.name: Liver
icons.description: Liver with falciform ligament and gallbladder.

icons.name: Intestines
icons.description: Small intestine framed by the large intestine (colon) with haustra, appendix and rectum.

icons.name: Skin
icons.description: Skin cross-section: epidermis, dermis with blood vessels, hair follicle and sweat gland, and subcutaneous fat.

icons.name: Bone
icons.description: Long bone with a window onto the marrow cavity.

icons.name: Knee joint
icons.description: Knee joint in section: femur, tibia and fibula with articular cartilage (blue) inside the synovial capsule (green).

icons.name: Lymph node
icons.description: Lymph node with follicles and germinal centres, afferent lymphatics, and efferent lymphatic, artery and vein at the hilum.

icons.name: Spleen
icons.description: Spleen with splenic artery and vein at the hilum.

icons.name: Thymus
icons.description: Bilobed, lobulated thymus.

icons.name: Ear
icons.description: Ear in section: pinna and external canal to the eardrum, the middle ear with the malleus, incus and stapes and the Eustachian tube, and the inner ear with the cochlea, vestibule and semicircular canals.

icons.name: Eye
icons.description: Eye in section, front to the left: cornea, iris, lens and ciliary body, the retina and choroid lining the globe, and the optic nerve and rectus muscles running back to the orbit.

icons.name: Placenta
icons.description: Placenta from the fetal side, with chorionic vessels branching from the umbilical cord, whose two arteries (deoxygenated, blue) coil round its vein.

icons.name: Heart valve with vegetations
icons.description: Aortic valve seen from above, its three cusps meeting along their closure lines, with bacterial vegetations on the cusps (infective endocarditis).

icons.name: Meninges
icons.description: Section through the scalp, skull, dura, arachnoid with trabeculae across the CSF-filled subarachnoid space, and the pia on the cortex, dipping into a sulcus.

icons.name: Antibiotic capsule
icons.description: Two-part oral capsule.

icons.name: IV infusion bag
icons.description: Labelled infusion bag with drip chamber and giving set tubing.

icons.name: Vaccine
icons.description: Vaccine vial with a syringe.

icons.name: Oral antibiotic suspension
icons.description: Amber medicine bottle with an oral dosing syringe, as used for liquid antibiotics in children.

icons.name: mRNA vaccine (lipid nanoparticle)
icons.description: Lipid nanoparticle with a lipid shell, PEG-lipids on the surface and mRNA inside.

icons.name: Antibiotic acting on the cell wall
icons.description: A β-lactam bound to a penicillin-binding protein (PBP), so the peptide cross-links between the glycan strands of the peptidoglycan wall are not made.

icons.name: Conjugate vaccine
icons.description: Capsular polysaccharide chains linked to a carrier protein (a toxoid such as CRM197 or tetanus toxoid), so the sugars draw a T-cell-dependent response.

icons.name: Viral-vector vaccine
icons.description: A harmless adenovirus vector, its capsid shown see-through, carrying DNA with an inserted gene for the target antigen.

icons.name: Monoclonal antibody injection
icons.description: A pre-filled syringe holding antibody, beside a large antibody, for a monoclonal antibody such as nirsevimab for RSV.

icons.name: Nasal-spray flu vaccine
icons.description: Nasal-spray applicator with its dose-divider clip, spraying a fine mist that carries live attenuated influenza virions.

icons.name: CAR T cell
icons.description: T cell bearing chimeric antigen receptors (scFv, hinge, and co-stimulatory and CD3ζ signalling domains), one of them binding CD19 on a target B cell.

icons.name: Oral rehydration solution
icons.description: A sachet of oral rehydration salts beside a mug of made-up solution.

icons.name: β-lactamase
icons.description: β-lactamase enzyme hydrolysing the β-lactam ring of an antibiotic in its active site.

icons.name: Efflux pump
icons.description: Efflux pump spanning the bacterial membrane, expelling antibiotic molecules.

icons.name: Antibiotic susceptibility plate
icons.description: Disc diffusion plate: antibiotic discs on a bacterial lawn, with zones of inhibition of different sizes and one resistant disc with none.

icons.name: Plasmid transfer
icons.description: Bacterial conjugation: a donor bacterium passes a copy of a plasmid carrying a resistance gene to a recipient through a mating bridge.

icons.name: MRSA (PBP2a)
icons.description: How MRSA resists β-lactams: a normal penicillin-binding protein is blocked by the drug, so the cell wall goes uncross-linked above it, while PBP2a, which β-lactams barely bind, carries on building it.

icons.name: Carbapenemase
icons.description: A Gram-negative cell envelope: carbapenems entering through porins are broken down by carbapenemase enzymes in the periplasm before they reach their target.

icons.name: Antimicrobial stewardship
icons.description: An antibiotic capsule inside a review cycle, with a tick.

icons.name: Blood culture bottle
icons.description: Inoculated blood culture bottle with label, barcode and base sensor.

icons.name: Blood agar plate
icons.description: Blood agar plate with colonies streaked out across quadrants, some surrounded by haemolysis.

icons.name: Child
icons.description: Young child standing.

icons.name: Newborn baby
icons.description: Swaddled newborn baby, seen from the front.

icons.name: Baby
icons.description: Baby sitting up, wearing a nappy.

icons.name: Thermometer
icons.description: Clinical thermometer showing a high reading.

icons.name: Stethoscope
icons.description: Stethoscope with earpieces, tubing and chest piece.

icons.name: Lumbar puncture
icons.description: Lumbar spine in side view with a needle between two spinous processes into the CSF-filled canal, and a drop of CSF.

icons.name: Nasopharyngeal swab
icons.description: Flocked swab with a tube of transport medium.

icons.name: Pregnant person
icons.description: Pregnant person in side view.

icons.name: IV cannula
icons.description: Peripheral intravenous cannula, seen from above: catheter, colour-coded wings and injection port, and a Luer-lock cap.

icons.name: PICC line
icons.description: Peripherally inserted central catheter with two lumens: the catheter, a junction hub with suture wings, and extension legs with clamps and needle-free connectors.

icons.name: Urine dipstick
icons.description: Urine sample pot beside a reagent strip with coloured test pads.

icons.name: Gram stain slide
icons.description: Microscope slide with a stained smear, and a magnified field showing violet Gram-positive cocci and pink Gram-negative bacilli.

icons.name: Lateral flow test
icons.description: Lateral flow test cassette with a sample well and a result window showing control and test lines (a positive result).

icons.name: Nebuliser mask
icons.description: Child-size face mask with a nebuliser chamber and oxygen tubing; also stands for an oxygen mask.

icons.name: Neonatal incubator
icons.description: Neonatal incubator with a clear hood, two portholes and a control unit, a swaddled baby lying inside.

icons.name: PCR tube
icons.description: PCR tube with an open hinged cap and reaction mix, beside a stretch of double-stranded DNA.

icons.name: Hand hygiene
icons.description: An open hand among soap bubbles and water drops.

icons.name: Face mask
icons.description: Pleated surgical face mask with ear loops and a nose wire.

icons.name: Parent and baby
icons.description: Adult holding a swaddled baby in their arms.

icons.name: Globe
icons.description: Globe with lines of latitude and longitude, circled by a flight path with an aeroplane.

icons.name: Blood bottles
icons.description: Adult blood tubes with coloured caps (EDTA purple, serum gold, citrate light blue, heparin green) and two paediatric microtubes with hinged caps.

icons.name: Microscope
icons.description: Compound light microscope with a slide on the stage.

icons.name: Glass test
icons.description: Glass pressed on skin with a purpuric rash: the skin blanches under the glass but the spots stay visible (a non-blanching rash).

icons.name: Chest X-ray
icons.description: Frontal (PA) chest radiograph: lung fields, ribs, clavicles, the heart shadow and the domes of the diaphragm.

icons.name: Pipette
icons.description: Single-channel micropipette with a disposable tip, dispensing a drop.

icons.name: 96-well plate
icons.description: A 96-well plate after an ELISA: two columns of standards fading in colour, then samples, yellow where positive.

icons.name: Centrifuge
icons.description: Benchtop microcentrifuge with its lid open, tubes loaded in balanced pairs in the rotor.

icons.name: Droplet transmission
icons.description: Large respiratory droplets passing from one person to another close by.

icons.name: Airborne transmission
icons.description: Fine aerosol particles carried on air currents from one person to another, and beyond.

icons.name: Contact transmission
icons.description: Bacteria passing from one hand to another by touch.

icons.name: Faecal–oral transmission
icons.description: The faecal–oral route as a cycle: from a nappy, to hands, to food or drink.

icons.name: Vector-borne transmission
icons.description: A mosquito carrying infection from one person to another.

icons.name: Vertical transmission
icons.description: A pregnant person with pathogens crossing the placenta to the fetus.
